tasks.prompt: I pulled some changes and want to know whether the project still typechecks. Check it and tell me the result. Don't change any files.

Add a read-only `isRetryable` getter to the `RestException` class in src/base/RestException.ts. It should return true when the status is 429 or any 5xx status, and false otherwise. Run the typecheck after the change. Then document the getter in README.md, in the "Using RestException for Better Error Handling" section, with a short example. Before you finish, confirm the project still typechecks.

When the Twilio API rate-limits a request it can send a Retry-After header. Add an optional `retryAfter?: number` property (seconds) to `RestException` in src/base/RestException.ts, set from the response's `retry-after` header when it is a non-negative integer, and left undefined otherwise. Header names may arrive in any case. Add unit tests for it to spec/unit/base/RestException.spec.ts. Make sure the typecheck and those tests pass.

The "Rendering" section of Readme.md shows `.html()`, `outerHTML` and `.text()`, but not XML output. Add a short paragraph with a small example showing how to render a document as XML with `$.xml()`. Before you finish, make sure the project still typechecks.
I pulled some changes and want to know whether the project still typechecks. Check it and tell me the result. Don't change any files.

Add jQuery-style `even()` and `odd()` methods to Cheerio selections in src/api/traversing.ts. Like jQuery 3.5, they use zero-based indexes: `even()` keeps elements 0, 2, 4, and so on, and `odd()` keeps 1, 3, 5. Both return a new selection, so `.end()` works. Run the typecheck after the change. Then mention the two methods in Readme.md's "Selectors" section with a one-line example. Before you finish, confirm the project still typechecks.

Add a `toggleAttr(name, force?)` method to Cheerio selections in src/api/attributes.ts. For each element, it removes the attribute when present and sets it to an empty string when absent. When `force` is given, `true` always sets it and `false` always removes it. It returns the selection for chaining. Add vitest tests to src/api/attributes.spec.ts. Make sure the typecheck and the tests pass.

The "TypeScript" section of README.md only shows string accessors. Add a short example showing that a function accessor such as `yAccessor={d => d.revenue}` is type-checked against the datum type too. Before you finish, make sure the project still typechecks.

In src/components/data/aggregateRows.ts, make `normalizeAggregate` accept "avg" as another alias for "mean", and match operation names case-insensitively, so "SUM" and "Mean" work. Run the typecheck after the change. Then add a line about it under "## [Unreleased]" in CHANGELOG.md, in a "### Changed" subsection. Before you finish, confirm the project still typechecks.

Add a `median` aggregate operation. Extend `AggregateOperation` and `normalizeAggregate` in src/components/data/aggregateRows.ts, and compute the median per group in `aggregateRows`, skipping missing values the same way `mean` does. The median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values. Add vitest tests to src/components/data/aggregation.test.ts. Make sure the typecheck and that test file pass (run only that test file; the full suite is slow).

The "Technical Details" section of README.md doesn't tell contributors how to check their changes. Add a bullet saying to run `npm run typecheck` before opening a pull request. Before you finish, make sure the project still typechecks.

In src/utils/parse-locale-number.ts, make `parseLocaleNumber` treat "none" as missing too, and match "unknown", "unavailable" and "none" case-insensitively, so "Unknown" and "NONE" return NaN. Run the typecheck after the change. Then add a line about it at the top of RELEASE_NOTES.md, under a new "## Unreleased" heading. Before you finish, confirm the project still typechecks.

Add an exported `parseLocalePercent(val: unknown): number` to src/utils/parse-locale-number.ts. It accepts the same inputs as `parseLocaleNumber`, plus strings with a trailing percent sign and optional space ("42%", "42,5 %"), and returns the number without the sign (42, 42.5); numbers pass through unchanged. Add vitest tests to src/utils/parse-locale-number.test.ts. Make sure the typecheck and that test file pass (run only that test file: `npx vitest run src/utils/parse-locale-number.test.ts`).

Add a short note to the "Backup" section of README.md saying to quit SwitchHosts before copying the `~/.SwitchHosts` folder, so the copy is consistent. Before you finish, make sure the project still typechecks.

In src/common/hostsFn.ts, make `extractDomain` return the domain in lower case, since domain names are case-insensitive ("GitHub.COM" becomes "github.com"). Run the typecheck after the change. Then add a sentence about it to the "Features" section of README.md. Before you finish, confirm the project still typechecks.

Add an exported `normalizeDomainList(list: string[]): string[]` to src/common/dns.ts. It trims each entry, drops entries that `extractDomain` rejects, uses the extracted domain in lower case, removes duplicates while keeping the first one, and keeps at most `MAX_DOMAINS` entries. Add vitest tests to src/common/dns.test.ts. Make sure the typecheck and that test file pass (run only that test file: `npx vitest --config ./vitest.config.mts --watch=false src/common/dns.test.ts`).
